subject: Post-call: Bridging econ for batching & cache at PayFrame
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martin <alex.martin@payframe.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Bridging econ for batching & cache at PayFrame

Alex — thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single place to align.

Recap of needs / pain points
- Monthly token spend is the blocker for pilot (you mentioned ~$28–35k/month).
- Peak latency requirement: 95th <= 350ms for customer-facing flows.
- Bursty traffic around batch settlement windows (daily spikes, ~2x baseline QPS).
- Need predictable unit economics to get procurement sign-off (3-month pilot -> buy).

Redwood levers we discussed (what moves the needle)
- Batching: combine small requests into continuous-batch windows to reduce per-request overhead. Expect ~20–35% unit cost reduction on request-heavy endpoints depending on request size.
- Prefix/KV caching: for repeated prompts (status checks, templated responses) we can cache prefix outputs — typically saves 10–25% tokens on chat-style flows.
- Model selection & quantization: switching to a quantized variant for non-critical paths gives 15–30% savings at modest latency lift.
- Routing policy: route >90% non-latency-critical traffic to cheaper variants/regions during spikes.

Initial sizing & hypothesis (rough)
- Current: ~1.2M tokens/day (customer estimate) -> ~36M tokens/month.
- Pilot target: 100k daily queries (mix avg token-length 40) -> ~4M tokens/month baseline.
- Hypothetical blended savings for pilot using batching + caching + quantized variants: 35–50% token reduction -> pilot estimate $12–20k/month (depending on SLO choices).

Attachments: I attached two files — an econ scenarios workbook with 3 sensitivity cases and a SOW draft for a 12-week pilot.
-- Attachment: payframe-econ-scenarios.xlsx (xlsx, 48KB)
-- Attachment: redwood-pilot-sow-draft.pdf (pdf, 62KB)

Suggested next steps
1) You confirm the monthly budget target that procurement will approve (you said ~$30k as a hard ceiling).
2) We run a brief usage profile export (QPS by hour, token length distribution, percent identical prompts) — if you can share an anonymized sample, Rishi and I can run the scenarios and lock numbers.
3) We deliver a 1-page pilot plan + final SOW and a prioritized list of levers (must-have vs nice-to-have).
4) Kick pilot: ~2 week setup, 8 week execution, then a decision window.

If that aligns, I’ll turn the workbook into a 2-slide exec summary for Procurement and update the SOW for signature.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Kimberly — appreciate the clear summary. A few quick clarifications from my side: 

- Budget: Procurement asked me to aim for <= $30k/month for the pilot (including whatever hosting/inference fees you show in the SOW).
- Latency: 95th <= 350ms is firm for the customer flow; for background reconciliation a slightly higher 95th is acceptable.
- Security: we need a short note in the SOW on data retention and log access (SOC2 controls) — procurement will want that up front.

I can share an anonymized traffic export for the last 30 days (we’ll strip PII). I will loop procurement on the SOW review; please include a one‑page pricing appendix with the econ scenarios so they can scan quickly.

Send me the revised SOW and the 1‑pager and I’ll get procurement to review Monday.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martin <alex.martin@payframe.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 24 Apr 2027 07:18:09 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Bridging econ for batching & cache at PayFrame

Thanks for the data offer — that will make the scenarios much tighter. Two quick engineering notes to set expectations on savings: 

- Batching impact depends heavily on request size distribution and tail latency targets. If most requests are tiny (<= 16 tokens input) and synchronous, continuous batching typically yields ~25% unit cost at 50–100ms batching windows; larger windows help more but worsen p95.
- KV/prefix caching effectiveness depends on hit rate. If you have ~30% identical prompts (or canonicalizable variants), you can expect 10–20% token reductions quickly; with templated user messages it can be higher.
- Quantized model variants reduce compute cost but can increase latency by 5–20ms; for background flows that’s usually fine.

To produce the procurement-friendly appendix I’ll need the following columns in your export (CSV is fine): timestamp, tokens_in, tokens_out, endpoint, is_streaming (y/n), region_origin. If you can share a sample slice (first 100k rows anonymized) I’ll run the three sensitivity scenarios and return a concise table: baseline spend, batch-only, batch+cache, batch+cache+quant.

I’m cc’ing an internal checklist I’ll run against the usage pattern:
- Percent requests < 20 tokens / avg token length
- Streaming vs non-streaming split
- Hourly QPS heatmap and peak factors

I’ll draft the pricing appendix and a short note on SOC2/data-retention language for the SOW.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
From: Alex Martin <alex.martin@payframe.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 24 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Bridging econ for batching & cache at PayFrame

Rishi / Kimberly — that all sounds good. I pulled a quick slice and the high-level numbers:
- Avg daily QPS (baseline): 1.6k (peaks to ~3.1k for ~20 minutes/day)
- Avg tokens_in per request: 28 tokens; avg tokens_out: 62 tokens
- Streaming endpoints are ~18% of traffic (mostly live chat flows)
- Approx 26% of requests are highly templated / repeated responses

Budget reminder: procurement has a hard cap of $30k/month for the pilot; we can trade scope (volume or SLOs) if needed to hit that number.

Next asks from us:
1) Prioritized levers with expected % savings and impact on latency (short table).
2) Updated SOW and 1-page pricing appendix (procurement-friendly).
3) A proposed kickoff date in the next 2 weeks (we prefer May 10 start).

If you can get the doc set to me by Monday morning P.T. I’ll route to procurement for sign-off.

Thanks — Alex
